bills.summary: Proof of citizenship required for all 13M+ registered Florida voters — mirrors SAVE Act. Also removes student IDs as valid voter ID. Takes effect Jan 1, 2027.
bills.status: SIGNED Apr 1 · Effective Jan 1, 2027 · Federal suits (NAACP, ACLU/LULAC) proceeding — no injunction as of Jul 30

bills.summary: State officials can designate nonprofits as 'domestic terrorist organizations' — no criminal conviction required. Bars state funding, criminalizes membership, expels public university students from designated orgs. Bans Sharia law in FL courts.
bills.status: SIGNED Apr 6 · In effect Jul 1 · CAIR suing · State says no designations until FDLE regulations finalized

bills.summary: Directs USPS to maintain national voter eligibility list and refuse to transmit mail ballots to anyone not on it. DHS and SSA ordered to create national voter database. Threatens states with criminal prosecution and funding cuts for noncompliance.
bills.status: Core provisions ENJOINED for 2026 (Talwani, Jun 25; Section 3 ruled unconstitutional Jul 23) · 1st Circuit refused stay Jul 25 · DOJ emergency application at SCOTUS (Trump v. California) — states respond by Aug 3

bills.summary: Eliminates countywide early voting — Fulton loses 43 sites, DeKalb loses 19. Assigns all voters to a single designated precinct. Mandates hand-marked paper ballots for November 2026 general only. Same sponsor is calling for Fulton County state takeover.
bills.status: DEAD — Failed Senate floor vote 27-21 (Mar 6) · Session ended without revival

bills.summary: Virginia joins the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact — awards VA's electoral votes to the national popular vote winner when enough states join.
bills.status: SIGNED by Gov. Spanberger (Apr 14) · VA joins NPV compact — 222 of 270 EVs

bills.summary: Proof of citizenship required for state elections only — creates two-tier voting system. Federal elections exempt. Kansas used same bifurcated approach: 31,000 voters blocked.
bills.status: SIGNED Mar 25 · In effect since May 6 · 5,000+ voters flagged for citizenship proof; nonresponders get federal-only ballots in Nov · State review found 27 confirmed noncitizens among 2M+ voters

bills.summary: Removes student IDs as valid voter identification — disproportionately affects college-town voters.
bills.status: SIGNED by Gov. Ayotte (early Apr) · In effect for 2026 elections

bills.summary: SF 2203 died at funnel; companion SF 2218 enacted instead: ANNUAL citizenship verification of every registered voter via the federal SAVE database. HF 2501 also eliminates the identity-attestation option.
Deploying federal troops or military personnel at New Mexico polling places is a fourth-degree felony. Also bars any attempt to alter voter qualifications beyond state law.
bills.status: Signed into law (Mar 9) · First state to ban armed federal agents at polls

bills.summary: SCR 1001 (killing the Active Early Voter List) stalled in the House. Legislature instead referred HCR 2001 'FAST Election Results Act' to the Nov 2026 ballot: government-issued ID for ALL voters including mail, on-site Election Day counting of dropped mail ballots. Effective 2028 if approved.
bills.status: HCR 2001 ON THE NOV 2026 BALLOT (referred Jun 13, party-line) · Counter-initiative gathering signatures

bills.summary: Creates a state-law right to sue federal officers (ICE, CBP, any federal agent) for constitutional violations in New York state courts. Directly fills the gap left by decades of Supreme Court rulings limiting Bivens claims.
bills.status: Amended to S8500B · Recommitted to Senate Codes (Feb 9) · Not passed as of Jul 30

bills.summary: Puts winner-take-all electoral college allocation on the November 2026 ballot — would eliminate the Omaha 'blue dot' district vote that has split Nebraska's electoral votes in 2008, 2020, and 2024.
bills.status: No floor vote reported before session end · Not among verified Nov 2026 ballot referrals — confirm final disposition

bills.bill: A-1715 / S-282 — John R. Lewis Voter Empowerment Act
bills.summary: State-level Voting Rights Act: preclearance for local voting changes, language access, and a state cause of action against vote denial or dilution — first state VRA enacted after Callais (11th overall).
